the following issues: (1) The geopolitical context of peacekeeping operations; (2) The political and economic interests of the UN, its member states and troop-contributing nations; (3) The political interests and objectives of the conflicting parties; (4) The political and social consequences of peacekeeping operations.

peacekeepers have been involved in a wide range of political activities in all the countries in which they have been deployed.
peacekeeping is a complex and multi-layered phenomenon.
UN peacekeepers are not “neutral”, and that they are not “apolitical”.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the political and social effects of peacekeeping are highly complex, often unpredictable and frequently contradictory.
peacekeepers are often caught in a web of contradictions, which is not of their own making.

peacekeeping missions have been successful in some areas and not so in others, and that the success or failure of a mission is often determined by a combination of factors, including the nature of the conflict, the political and economic interests of the major powers, and the nature of the peacekeeping force itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
peacekeepers are political actors, who have a profound influence on the landscapes and communities within which they operate.
peacekeepers are not simply neutral actors in the conflict landscapes they enter.
